name: Safran Aircraft Engines

what_it_is.prose: Safran Aircraft Engines is the propulsion arm of France's Safran S.A. and one of the world's largest aero-engine makers; it develops the M88 fighter engine, is CFM International's partner on the LEAP commercial engine (with GE), and anchors the Safran group's deep and expanding India footprint of roughly 3,000–3,500 employees across 18 sites built over more than 70 years. Its most direct Indian military relevance is the M88 turbofan, which powers the Indian Air Force's Rafale fighters (36 delivered) and will power the 26 naval Rafale-M on order; Safran has opened a dedicated M88 MRO shop in Hyderabad (over €40 million, ~5,000 m², capacity for 600+ engine modules a year, supporting Rafale and Mirage 2000) and is in discussions on progressively localising M88 assembly to meet indigenous-content targets under the wider MRFA fighter competition. Alongside it, Safran opened a €200 million LEAP-engine MRO facility in Hyderabad (~45,000 m², 300 shop visits a year, up to 1,100 jobs at full capacity) — India being CFM's third-largest LEAP market with 400-plus LEAP-powered aircraft and 2,000 engines on order. On rotorcraft, Safran (through Safran Helicopter Engines) co-developed the Ardiden 1H1 'Shakti' with HAL — powering HAL's Dhruv (ALH), Light Combat Helicopter and Light Utility Helicopter — and in August 2024 finalised the 50/50 SAFHAL Helicopter Engines joint venture with HAL to develop and produce the ~1,500 kW-class Aravalli engine for India's future Indian Multi-Role Helicopter (IMRH) and Deck-Based Multi-Role Helicopter (DBMRH). Safran has stated it will triple its India revenue to more than €3 billion by 2030, half generated locally, and is in talks with India on a clean-sheet fighter engine for the AMCA. Note on scope: the group's helicopter-engine work (Shakti, Aravalli/SAFHAL) sits under Safran Helicopter Engines, a sibling company within Safran, while the M88 and LEAP MRO are Safran Aircraft Engines proper; this dossier treats the Safran-group aero-propulsion presence as one entity while flagging the internal division.

deployments_procurement.summary: Safran's Indian propulsion footprint runs across fighter, commercial and helicopter engines and is increasingly local: M88 engines power the IAF Rafale and 26 naval Rafale-M; a dedicated M88 MRO and a €200M LEAP MRO are operational in Hyderabad; the SAFHAL JV with HAL is developing the Aravalli helicopter engine; and the Shakti/Ardiden co-production with HAL already powers Indian rotorcraft fleets. Safran plans to more than triple India revenue past €3bn by 2030.

import_dependencies.summary: Safran's Indian engine business currently rests on foreign design authority: the M88, LEAP and Ardiden/Shakti cores are French-designed, with India's value-add concentrated in MRO (Hyderabad LEAP and M88 shops), Shakti co-production and the planned Aravalli JV. Hot-section technology, single-crystal turbine blades, FADEC and the core design IP remain with Safran in France until localization and the SAFHAL/AMCA programmes mature.

faq.question: Which Indian aircraft use Safran engines?
faq.answer: The Safran M88 turbofan powers the Indian Air Force's Rafale fighters (36 delivered) and will power the 26 naval Rafale-M on order. The Safran-HAL Ardiden 1H1 'Shakti' powers HAL's Dhruv (ALH), Light Combat Helicopter and Light Utility Helicopter; Safran says more than 1,200 of its helicopter engines are in service with the Indian armed forces.

faq.question: What engine MRO does Safran run in India?
faq.answer: Safran has opened two engine MRO shops in Hyderabad: a €200 million LEAP-engine facility (about 45,000 m², capacity for 300 shop visits a year and up to 1,100 jobs at full capacity) and a more than €40 million M88 fighter-engine module shop (about 5,000 m², 600+ modules a year, up to 150 jobs) supporting Rafale and Mirage 2000. PM Modi inaugurated the facility in November 2025.

faq.question: What is the SAFHAL / Aravalli helicopter-engine joint venture?
faq.answer: SAFHAL Helicopter Engines is a 50/50 joint venture between Safran Helicopter Engines and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, whose final contract was signed on 30 August 2024. It will develop and produce the ~1,500 kW-class Aravalli engine to power India's future 13-tonne Indian Multi-Role Helicopter (IMRH) and Deck-Based Multi-Role Helicopter (DBMRH). This work sits under Safran Helicopter Engines, a sibling company of Safran Aircraft Engines within the Safran group.
